meta.title: GLP-1 Agonists Are Associated With a Significant Reduction in Breast Cancer Incidence in Women.
meta.abstract:
Purpose

Excess weight is a key modifiable risk factor for breast cancer. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1) promote weight loss and improve metabolic health, but their effect on breast cancer risk remains unclear.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study from January 1, 2022, to June 30, 2025, using electronic health records. We identified 217,624 unique women who underwent breast imaging; restricting to ages 45-80 years with a BMI ≥25 and a documented imaging outcome (n = 111,646; median age 61 years). The primary outcome was breast cancer detection. GLP-1 use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date and assessed in relation to race, ethnicity, age, and type 2 diabetes. To address potential confounding between these covariates and GLP-1 exposure, we performed one-to-one, case-control matching using propensity scores on the basis of age, race, ethnicity, highest BMI, breast density, and history of type 2 diabetes. The propensity matching to the GLP-1 use group was performed using the greedy nearest neighbor approach.

Results

GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer (odds ratio [OR], 0.649 [95% CI, 0.569 to 0.741]; P < .0001). In the matched logistic regression (30,528 observations; 600 cancer cases), GLP-1 exposure was associated with a lower breast cancer incidence (OR, 0.695 [95% CI, 0.590 to 0.819]; P < .0001).

Conclusion

In this large observational study of women undergoing breast imaging at a major academic center and affiliated sites, GLP-1 treatment was associated with a lower incidence of breast cancer, independent of age, race, ethnicity, BMI, breast density, and diabetes. The findings support the need for prospective trials investigating GLP-1 agonists for breast cancer prevention.

Furthermore, critical breast cancer risk factors (family history, parity, age at menarche/menopause, hormone replacement therapy) were unmeasured and omitted from matching.

domains.name: Measurement of the exposure
domains.direction_justification: Defining exposure as a single prescription prior to the imaging examination date without imposing a biologically plausible latency window (lag-time) or cumulative dose threshold counts patients with trivial, recent, or non-adherent exposure as 'protected', generating an immediate protective association (OR 0.695) over a brief 3.5-year study window (2022-2025) that is biologically incompatible with primary breast carcinogenesis.

findings.title: Absence of induction/latency period and duration requirement
findings.mechanism: A single prescription issued shortly before imaging cannot plausibly prevent solid tumor initiation or progression to detection within months, reflecting immortal time/protopathic artifacts rather than causal pharmacology.
evidence: GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date (Page 2, Methods)
We did not specifically examine the impact of exposure duration or drug dosage... We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy (Page 7, Discussion)

findings.title: Unverified adherence and out-of-system exposure
findings.mechanism: Prescription orders in EHR do not reflect dispensed medications or adherence, and out-of-system/compounded formulations lead to unmeasured exposure misclassification.
evidence: There could be patients on GLP-1 agonists who obtained these drugs outside of our health system... compounding pharmacies (Page 7, Discussion)

findings.title: Absence of lag period and unaddressed biological latency
findings.mechanism: Cancers detected at or shortly after GLP-1 initiation existed as preclinical lesions long before drug exposure; without a lag period, any immediate difference in diagnosis cannot be attributed to biological prevention.
evidence: GLP-1 agonist use was defined as a first prescription before the examination date
We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy, because exposure is not definitely related to dose

findings.title: Lack of new-user active comparator cohort and immortal lookback time
findings.mechanism: Defining exposure cross-sectionally relative to an imaging exam date allows prevalent users and creates an immortal interval between initial prescription and imaging where cancer detection was structurally precluded.

domains.direction_justification: Conditioning cohort inclusion on undergoing breast imaging (n=217,624 reduced to 111,646) induces collider stratification bias. GLP-1 users undergo imaging during routine metabolic management, whereas unexposed women disproportionately undergo imaging for diagnostic workups or elevated clinical suspicion, leading to a higher cancer detection rate in controls (2.31% vs 1.62%).

findings.mechanism: Restricting the cohort strictly to individuals undergoing breast imaging distorts the risk ratio because the indication for imaging (routine screening vs diagnostic evaluation of symptoms) differs systematically by GLP-1 prescription status.

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: Exclusions due to missing BMI or missing imaging outcomes occurred prior to cohort matching, and all matched pairs (n=30,528) had complete data for the analyzed variables.

findings.mechanism: Patients without recorded BMI or documented imaging outcome were excluded upfront (54,799 excluded for BMI < 25 or unrecorded).

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Outcome was defined objectively via histopathology diagnosis of malignancy (247 cases in GLP-1 vs 353 cases in matched control), though out-of-system cancer diagnoses not captured in the health system EHR could cause minor non-differential outcome underascertainment.

evidence: The primary outcome was a malignant breast pathology diagnosis during the study period (Page 2, Methods)

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Retrospective EHR analysis without a published pre-registered protocol or pre-specified statistical analysis plan leaves flexibility in matching algorithms and covariate selection.

findings.title: Absence of pre-registered analysis plan
findings.mechanism: Model choices (greedy nearest neighbor on logit propensity score vs multivariable adjustment, definition of BMI as maximum historical BMI from 2017-2025) were determined retrospectively.
evidence: BMI was a maximum for each patient during the time period from January 1, 2017, to June 30, 2025 (Page 2, Methods)

overall.summary: This retrospective observational study demonstrates a substantial risk of bias that invalidates causal conclusions. The observed 30.5% odds reduction (matched OR 0.695) is driven by critical methodological flaws: (1) exposure defined simply as any single prescription before imaging without a required latency/lag period or cumulative exposure threshold in a short 3.5-year window; (2) selection bias induced by restricting exclusively to patients undergoing breast imaging; and (3) residual confounding from unmatched baseline breast cancer history (7.8% in controls vs 5.9% in GLP-1 users) and unmeasured reproductive/familial risk factors. These biases systematically push the effect estimate away from the null.

baseline_comparability.summary: Although the GLP-1 exposed cohort had a much higher general comorbidity burden, the unexposed control group had a higher baseline prevalence of prior breast cancer (7.8% vs 5.9% in the matched set) and higher breast density, which were not fully controlled for. This residual imbalance in key oncologic risk factors biases the observed effect away from the null.

lag_and_latency.follow_up_vs_latency: The entire study window was 3.5 years (January 1, 2022, to June 30, 2025; derived: 42 months), with no minimum duration required and no lag applied, whereas solid tumor breast carcinogenesis has a biological latency typically requiring 5 to 10+ years to manifest clinically or radiographically.

duration_gradient.interpretation: The authors explicitly acknowledge that they did not assess cumulative dose or duration ('we did not specifically examine the impact of exposure duration or drug dosage on cancer development. We also did not require a minimum duration of therapy'). Consequently, the analysis cannot differentiate a true causal biological prevention from protopathic bias, reverse causation, or screening artifacts.

time_related_biases.summary: The study defines exposure as any prior prescription before an imaging exam without an inception cohort, washout, or lag period within a maximum 3.5-year observation window. This temporal design allows reverse causation and immortal time to bias the effect estimate strongly toward an apparent reduction in breast cancer risk.
